=== page 4 ===
Diageo India (United Spirits Limited) is among India’s 
leading beverage alcohol (alcobev) companies with a portfolio of premium brands. A subsidiary of Diageo Plc., it is listed in India on both the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) as United Spirits Limited (USL). Headquartered in Bengaluru, the Company manufactures, sells and distributes an outstanding collection of iconic Global and Indian brands, blending global expertise with local innovation to deliver world-class products and experiences to consumers. 
As USL leads and shapes the future of the alcobev industry 
in India, we remain equally committed to building a more sustainable, progressive, and inclusive world. Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) focus is at the heart of our business strategy, as outlined in our ‘Spirit of Progress’ agenda. This agenda is focused on pioneering grain-to-glass sustainability, championing inclusion and diversity, and promoting positive drinking all underpinned by doing business the right way.

Reporting Period and Scope
All the financial and non-financial information presented in the 
report pertains to USL (unless otherwise stated) for the reporting period April 1, 2024 - March 31, 2025. We provide historical trends, wherever relevant, of the key performance indicators (KPIs), including those relating to ESG metrics, to give readers a complete understanding of our value-creation process. 
Reporting Framework, Guidelines and 
Standards
This report should be read together with the annual accounts 
(pages 305 to 490) for a complete understanding of our financial performance. 
The narrative section of the Report adheres to the International 
Integrated Reporting Council’s (IIRC) <IR> Framework guidelines. It provides an overview of our performance and business activities.
The statutory sections, comprising the Board’s Report, 
Management Discussion and Analysis (MDA), Corporate Governance Report, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) and Financial Statements, comply with/reports on/references the following:
• Companies Act, 2013 and its associated rules
• Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations of 2015, and the revised Secretarial Standards issued by The Institute of Company Secretaries of India
• Indian Accounting Standards (IND AS)
• National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC)
• United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs)United Spirits Limited
Our Capitals 
FINANCIAL CAPITAL
Refers to the financial resources we generate or raise through 
external sources, which are strategically and prudently deployed across our operations to create long-term value and deliver returns for our stakeholders.
HUMAN CAPITAL
Represents the passion, talent, and customer-first mindset of our people. We invest in their development and foster an equitable, inclusive, and safe work culture. By encouraging creativity, innovation, and independent thinking, we empower our teams to drive performance and strengthen our position as one of the leading alcobev company.
SOCIAL AND RELATIONSHIP CAPITAL
Represents the trust and long-standing relationships we have built with our stakeholders. Actively engaging with them, addressing their concerns, and fostering long-term partnerships are integral to our business strategy and long-term success. These relationships are essential to upholding our reputation and securing our licence to operate.
NATURAL CAPITAL
Represents the natural resources — such as water, energy, and agricultural inputs — that are essential to our operations, along with the environmental impact of our activities. Through our focus on driving ‘Grain to Glass Sustainability’, we are advancing key environmental goals and ensuring our operations remain responsible and sustainable.BRAND CAPITAL
Reflects the strong reputation, consumer trust, and emotional connection that Diageo India enjoys in the market. Our focus on building a portfolio of innovative, premium brands — supported by impactful marketing and brand-building campaigns — continues to enhance our brand perception and strengthen our market position.
MANUFACTURED CAPITAL
Represents our network of plants, equipment, and logistics infrastructure. We continuously invest — both organically and inorganically — to expand our assets and adopt global best practices and technologies. This enables us to produce and deliver high-quality spirits efficiently, safely, and sustainably to our customers and consumers.
INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL
Encompasses our deep expertise in processes, technologies, and the craft of spirit-making that sets us apart in the industry and fuels innovation. We consistently invest in creating disruptive, sustainable products and enhancing our manufacturing, logistics, and sales capabilities. Our ongoing digital transformation is shaping a future-ready organisation.Materiality Determination 
We identify and prioritise material issues that may impact 
our business and stakeholder value by engaging with key stakeholders and business units. These insights help shape strategy and ensure relevance in a dynamic environment.
Assurance
Financial information: The financial statements presented in the Report have been audited by Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP.
Selected non-financial performance metrics:  Reasonable 
Assurance of BRSR Core Indicators have been provided by Price 
Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP. The scope and basis of assurance are stated in the Assurance report issued by Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP.
All other financial and non-financial performance information: 
Internally verified and assured by the Management of the Company.
Forward-Looking Statement 
Certain statements in the Report regarding our business operations 
may constitute forward-looking statements. While these statements reflect our future expectations, it is important to be mindful that some of the risks, uncertainties and other important factors could cause actual results to differ materially from our expectations.

About the Report
This is the first Integrated Annual Report of United Spirits Limited (USL) 
(or ‘Diageo India’ or ‘the Company’), developed in line with the guiding principles of the Integrated Reporting <IR> framework overseen by the IFRS Foundation. 
USL believes in making disclosures that go beyond the statutory requirements. This report, covering both financial and non-financial performance, presents information on how we run the business and our approach to value creation and key outcomes for the stakeholders. Additionally, we present information on our business model, material matters, risks and opportunities, strategy, governance, performance, and outlook. Such holistic disclosures equip the providers of financial capital and other stakeholders with relevant information for informed decision-making.

04 | Integrated Annual Report 2024–25 05Progress is not just about achieving milestones

=== page 7 ===
People, Sustainability, and Governance
Our success is rooted in the strength of our iconic brands 
and the exceptional talent within Diageo India. We are committed to nurturing this talent by fostering an inclusive environment where diversity thrives, and every individual can contribute their best. Your Company continues to build an organisation of the future by nurturing talent, driving digital transformation, and embedding sustainability into every aspect of its operations. A range of initiatives were introduced this year to accelerate leadership development, deepen inclusion and diversity, and enhance employee engagement, reinforcing your Company’s position as a top employer. 
Sustainability remains at the core of your Company’s long-
term vision. With significant achievements across its ‘Spirit of Progress’ ESG action plan, your Company is leading industry efforts in water stewardship, renewable energy adoption, circularity, and regenerative agriculture. 
At the foundation of this progress is a strong governance 
framework, ensuring that business is conducted with integrity, transparency, and responsibility. This commitment to ethical leadership reinforces your Company’s long-term value creation strategy.
A Future-Focused Vision
The macroeconomic environment has become ever more complex and volatile. Globally, political and economic uncertainty, shifts in trade policies and tariffs, fluctuating commodity prices, and currency volatility have created challenges for businesses. In India, companies across sectors 
are grappling with changes such as in inflationary 
pressures and supply chain uncertainties, and their impact on consumer choice and demand. But the long-term potential of India’s beverage alcohol industry remains strong, driven by the country’s economic transformation, rising affluence, and evolving consumer aspirations. Your Company is well-positioned to harness these opportunities through a disciplined focus on premiumisation, innovation, and purpose-led growth.
In addition, the new Free Trade Agreement recently announced by 
the UK and India government will reduce tariffs in many industries, with whisky being one of the major beneficiaries. India is the world’s largest whisky market, with Diageo India being a leading player with a wide array of brands, and this landmark treaty will enable improved accessibility of Scotch for Indian consumers and boost the growth of alcobev and hospitality industries. 
I extend my deepest gratitude to Diageo Plc, our employees, 
partners, customers, and shareholders for their continuous support and trust. Together we will continue to deliver exceptional experiences to our consumers and make a positive impact on our communities. 
Thank you for being part of this exciting journey.Warm Regards, 
V K Viswanathan  
ChairpersonChairperson’s Message
Dear Shareholders,
In the past year , Diageo India has 
demonstrated resilience, agility and an unwavering commitment to delivering value for all our stakeholders with the belief that success is not just about financial performance, it is about anticipating consumer shifts, fostering a culture of innovation, strengthening partnerships and making a meaningful impact on society. By all these measures, FY 2024-25 was another year of purposeful progress for your Company.Performance Review
In FY 2024-25, your company registered a healthy financial 
performance, achieving its growth targets, including double-digit growth in the Prestige & Above (P&A) segment. Profitability remained healthy, with consolidated PAT of ` 1,582 Crores and a net profit margin of 13.1%. Standalone PAT stood at ` 1,558 Crores with a net profit margin of 13.5%, expanding by 119 bps year-on-year. 
The Board of Directors has recommended an interim 
dividend of ` 4 per share for FY 2024-25, underscoring our commitment to delivering sustained shareholder value. The Board has also recommended a final dividend of ` 8 per 
share subject to Shareholders’ approval for FY 2024-25.
Board and Leadership Changes
Towards the end of FY 2024-25, Hina Nagarajan, Managing Director and CEO, was appointed as President, Diageo Africa. On behalf of the Board, I extend my sincere appreciation to Hina for her outstanding leadership and strategic vision over the past four years. Under her stewardship, Diageo India accelerated its premiumisation agenda, strengthened its market position through innovative offerings, and became debt-free for the first time since acquisition. She was also instrumental in supporting the Indian alcobev startup ecosystem through strategic investments in brands such as Greater Than, Hapusa Gins, Quaffine Coffee Liqueur, Sober Non-Alcoholic Spirits, and Pistola Craft Agave Spirits. 
I am pleased to welcome Praveen Someshwar as 
Managing Director and CEO of Diageo India. Praveen is a dynamic business leader with over three decades of experience in driving business transformation, strategy, and execution within the media and FMCG industries. With a sharp strategic mindset and a strong focus on executional excellence, his leadership will be pivotal as your Company enters its next phase of growth. 
I would also like to welcome the three new directors who 
have been inducted to the board. Dr. Indu Bhushan, Amrita Gangotra and Mukesh Bhutani bring varied skills, competencies and expertise that will strongly support our growth agenda.

Managing Director & CEO’s Message
Dear Shareholders,
It has been a privilege to step into the 
role of Managing Director & CEO of Diageo India. Over the last few months, I’ve had the opportunity to immerse myself in the vibrant world of beverage alcohol, and I must say — this is a business like no other .
The passion surrounding our brands, the pride in our legacy, 
and our potential to shape culture and consumer experiences is inspiring. I have had the invaluable opportunity to work closely with my predecessors, Hina Nagarajan and M K Sharma, and I extend my deepest gratitude to them for their outstanding leadership. 
Having led high-impact consumer businesses, I find Diageo India’s 
sharp focus on premiumisation, innovation, and purpose-led growth a compelling proposition. I am excited to build on this strong foundation and gear the Company into its next curve of growth. 
Before diving into our performance, I want to spotlight something 
that truly stands out — our People and Culture. The level of ambition, inclusion, and collaboration across the organisation is nothing short of inspiring. Our commitment to fostering a diverse 
and inclusive environment has been integral to our success. It’s no surprise that we’ve been recognised among the top 20 companies globally for gender equality by Equileap and were named a Gold Employer for LGBTQIA+ inclusion for the second year in a row by the India Workplace Equality Index. 
Performance in a Changing Environment 
FY 2024-25 was a year of strong delivery and bold resets. We delivered impressive topline growth, expanded margins, and upheld profitability; even as broader market conditions turned more challenging. This performance is a testament to our resilient portfolio, disciplined execution, and future-ready mindset, as we navigated a complex macroeconomic landscape. Urban consumption slowed, and momentum at the top end of our portfolio moderated — but we stayed ahead through sharp revenue growth management, productivity unlocks, and continued investments in innovation, brands, and experiences. 
For the fiscal year, consolidated net sales reached ` 12,069 Crores, 
reflecting 6.6% growth, while standalone net sales grew 8.2% to ` 11,573 Crores. The Prestige & Above (P&A) segment grew by 9.9%, contributing 88.5% to net sales. Consolidated EBITDA grew by 12.1%, while standalone EBITDA rose 20.5% to ` 2,058 Crores. Profitability remained healthy, with consolidated PAT of ` 1,582 Crores and a net profit margin of 13.1%. Standalone PAT stood at ` 1,558 Crores with a margin of 13.5%, expanding by 119 bps year-on-year. 
Our operating model proved resilient. Smart execution across 
pricing, portfolio, and productivity helped us absorb external pressures and sustain momentum. These outcomes affirm the strength of our strategy, and our readiness to course-correct with confidence when needed. We remained consistent in shareholder returns. The Board approved an interim dividend of ` 4 per share, 
paid in April 2025, and has recommended a final dividend of ` 8 
per share, subject to shareholder approval. 
Looking ahead, we remain cautiously optimistic in the short-term 
while remaining committed to the long-term potential of the Indian consumer story. As we enter a new fiscal, we do so with clarity and conviction. The consumer is evolving, and we are evolving with them. More importantly, we’re not just navigating change; we’re positioned to lead and win. 
Building the Future of Spirits 
Whisky remains our most powerful growth engine. This year, we focused on transforming our portfolio through premiumisation, while tapping into evolving consumer trends and new segments. We strengthened our Scotch portfolio, with Johnnie Walker expanding its appeal across price points and lifestyles, scaling innovations like Johnnie Walker Blonde to engage younger LDA consumers. Black Dog underwent a contemporary reinvention, boosting its relevance and leadership in the international whisky category. Black & White tapped into new consumer preferences with an accessible liquid crafted for easy, food-paired moments, rooted in inclusion and genuine connection.Building on this momentum, we advanced our whisky agenda 
with Godawan, our artisanal Indian single malt and the most awarded Indian whisky globally with over 85 international awards. Godawan also made its debut in the UK, marking a defining moment for Indian whisky on the global stage. The launch of McDowell’s & Co Distiller’s Batch Indian Single Malt introduced a new era of triple cask matured craftsmanship. We also unlocked a new frontier in luxury with India Rare Spirits — the country’s first personalised cask programme featuring rare blends and bespoke packaging for the evolved Indian consumer.
Tequila is shaping up to be the next big growth opportunity. We 
made a decisive move with the launch of Don Julio, one of the world’s most iconic tequila brands, now introduced to Indian consumers with multiple variants. Early consumer response has been promising, and we see a clear runway to establish and lead this emerging category. 
In white spirits, our innovations have gained significant momentum. 
McDowell’s X Series has reimagined the category with a curated range of vodkas, gins, and rums, crafted for the cocktail-forward consumer. Smirnoff continues to drive flavour-led experimentation, with Mirchi Mango, Minty Jamun, and Zesty Lime variants now scaled across key markets. These innovations are not just expanding our portfolio, they’re reshaping cocktail culture and repertoire drinking. 
We also continued to build brand experience beyond the bottle. 
From Lollapalooza to global icon Dua Lipa’s India debut and the India Cocktail Week, our brands showed up at the intersection of music, culture, and community. Beyond being touchpoints, these events are powerful brand-building platforms that drive aspiration and emotional connection with consumers. 
Our innovation journey is also ecosystem driven. With the launch 
of The Good Craft Co. (TGCC), we created a platform for India’s most exciting craft spirits and creators to immerse into the art and science behind spirits. TGCC is not just an experience home, it’s a cultural movement that’s raising the bar for homegrown craft excellence. Through Ventures, Diageo India’s investment arm, our strategic investments in startups like Nao Spirits, Pistola, Sober and Quaffine is helping shape the next wave of premium, responsible, and lifestyle-aligned brands. Together, TGCC and Ventures are strengthening India’s alcobev ecosystem and unlocking future-forward growth. 
Digitalisation & Execution Excellence 
Our digital transformation is progressing rapidly, with a clear focus on backend efficiencies and front-end innovation. On the backend, we are optimising processes, building efficiencies, and driving operational leverage, delivering strong results. A prime example of this is our re-entry into Andhra Pradesh, where we combined speed, precision, and on-ground execution to capture growth in a complex market. 
At the front-end, we are laying the foundation for building a 
strong community of bartenders and customers. We’ve scaled up our first-party data capabilities to enable more personalised communication and deeper consumer engagement. By leveraging data science, automation, and predictive analytics, we are driving efficiencies across our marketing spends. This approach allows us to deliver smarter, more targeted campaigns, aligning our offerings to consumer needs, and ultimately optimising our investments.Driving Progress in ESG 
As a leading voice in the alcobev industry, we are committed to 
changing the way India drinks, for the better. Positive Drinking is a business priority, embedded across our brands, experiences, and consumer touchpoints, encouraging consumers to drink better, not more. We are also investing in education-led behaviour change. Initiatives like Act Smart India and Wrong Side of the Road address underage drinking and drink-driving, while our DRINKiQ platform empowers consumers with the knowledge to make smart, informed choices. 
We are delivering bold outcomes with clarity and confidence 
on 
grain-to-glass sustainability . We have eliminated coal from 
all our distilleries, marking a significant milestone in sustainable manufacturing. We’ve reduced our greenhouse gas emissions by 93% and transitioned to 99% renewable energy in direct operations since FY 2020. 
Our water stewardship efforts are industry leading: we’ve 
replenished over 1.1 million cubic metres of water, exceeding our targets three years ahead of schedule. Water-use efficiency has improved by 54% in distillation and 35% in packaging from  FY 2020 baseline. Our Alwar distillery remains the only one in Asia certified by the Alliance for Water Stewardship, underscoring our leadership in water-positive practices. We are also a founding member of The Godavari Initiative, a multi-stakeholder collaborative for promoting sustainable management of the Godavari River Basin in Maharashtra. 
We are embedding circularity across the value chain. Our 
packaging innovations — ranging from light-weighting and PET bottles to eliminating mono-cartons from 95% of our portfolio, have helped reduce waste and carbon emissions. Beyond direct operations, we continue to engage suppliers to reduce Scope 3 emissions and accelerate the shift to low-carbon materials and technologies. Our ESG performance is drawing strong investor interest, with sustainability ratings that are among the highest in the CPG industry. 
Diversity and inclusion remain central to our growth agenda and 
goes beyond the organisation. Our ‘Learning for Life’ programme has trained 1,922 youth, including Persons with Disabilities (PwDs), for careers in the hospitality industry, with more than 50% of them being women. 
Poised for the Future 
We are proud partners in driving the bold transformation that India is witnessing as we work towards ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047. We’ve created 1,00,000+ direct jobs, supported 3,75,000 allied livelihoods. Today, our brands are exported to 24 countries, taking Indian pride to the world, as we gear up for the future in the ‘consumer market of the next decade’.
At Diageo India, we’re not just responding to change, we’re 
shaping it. As we continue this journey, I’m energised by the passion of our people, the power of our brands, and the trust of our stakeholders. We’re driving spirited progress, inspired by purpose. 
This is the business of better, and we’re proud to lead the way. 
Warm Regards, 
Praveen Someshwar 
Managing Director & CEO

Our Approach to Stakeholder Engagement 
Stakeholder engagement at Diageo India is guided by our 
materiality assessment process, ensuring we focus on the most relevant and impactful issues. We maintain continuous dialogue and feedback with stakeholders to prioritise key areas such as environmental stewardship, social equity, governance, product innovation, and financial performance, aligning our strategy with the evolving expectations of stakeholders. We believe in governance that upholds the interests of the Company while creating value for both shareholders and stakeholders. A cross-functional Diageo India Leadership Team (DILT), comprising functional heads, communicates stakeholder expectations to the Executive Committee, led by the Managing Director and CEO. The Executive Committee, in consultation with the Board, makes the necessary decisions to address stakeholder interests. Key Stakeholders

An in-depth analysis of our material topics is the bedrock of our ESG and 
risk management strategy. It enables us to effectively respond to emerging ESG trends, and changing stakeholders’ perspectives. Additionally, the insights gained from this analysis help us align with globally recognised ESG standards, benchmarks, and disclosure frameworks, strengthening trust with shareholders and stakeholders. Prioritising the Issues that Matter MATERIALITY ASSESSMENT
Approach to Materiality Assessment
In 2020, we launched our ‘Spirit of Progress’ ESG action plan, 
aligning it with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs). The plan was informed by a comprehensive materiality assessment conducted in 2019 by our Global team at Diageo Plc, in collaboration with its global entities, including Diageo India. The assessment examined external trends influencing our operating environment and involved extensive engagement with diverse internal and external stakeholders. Their perspectives and findings were prioritised through workshops held with multiple business functions, including India. The process and outcomes were subsequently reviewed and finalised through deliberations with the Executive Committee and our Board. 
In FY 2023-24, we reviewed our material issues in consultation with 
both internal and external stakeholders, to stay attuned to shifts in the business landscape and stakeholder perceptions. The insights from the materiality exercise are incorporated into our business strategies and priorities to drive lasting value creation.

Diageo India’s ambition is to become the best-performing, most 
trusted, and respected consumer products company in India. We believe effective risk management begins with the right conversations that enable better business decisions. We identify material risks that could affect our current or future performance and reputation, and embed appropriate mitigation measures. Our approach is holistic and integrated, combining internal controls, business integrity, and risk oversight to focus on risks with the greatest potential impact. It is also structured to ensure we take all reasonable steps to mitigate, though not necessarily eliminate, our principal risks.
Risk management is embedded in our corporate strategy, which 
focuses on building a portfolio of world-class businesses that align organisational capabilities with market opportunities. It is further supported by structured succession planning, the development of specialist expertise, and timely interventions to enhance organisational capability.
As part of our journey towards risk intelligence, we have 
established a robust governance structure across the organisation. Given the nature of the business, it is exposed to various risks at different points in time. These include rising costs of raw materials

RISK MANAGEMENT  
OBJECTIVESand other inputs, increasing competitive intensity, regulatory changes at the central and state levels, as well as risks related to cybersecurity, data management and migration, data privacy, and environmental and climate challenges.
We have consistently maintained a proactive approach to risk 
management, conducting periodic reviews and developing appropriate mitigation measures. To further strengthen this focus, the Board of Directors has constituted a Risk Management Committee to frame, implement, and monitor the Company’s risk management plan.
Our Approach
We have identified and assessed risks, determining their expected impact and likelihood of occurring over medium to long term, using various parameters such as brand and reputation management, operational performance, people and workplace safety, and the potential financial impact on profit.

external environment and the emergence of new risks. At Diageo India, risk is defined as ‘an uncertainty that could help or hinder the achievement of our business objectives.’ Risk management encompasses all activities undertaken to identify, assess, manage, and report on risks.

All business functions follow a coordinated risk management process that uses a common language and approach to either mitigate risks or reduce their impact. India’s alcoholic beverage industry is poised for exponential growth, fuelled 
by rising incomes, rapid urbanisation, and evolving consumer aspirations. At Diageo India, we are actively shaping this transformation through innovation, portfolio premiumisation, and enhanced digital engagement – creating elevated experiences and expanding our consumer base. With significant headroom for growth, we are strongly positioned to capitalise on these trends and drive long-term growth and value creation.
Industry Context
India is poised to become the world’s third-largest economy and consumer market by 2030, underpinned by its youthful, rapidly expanding 
population, and long-term structural strengths. Over the past 5 years, the country has led global spirits volume growth contributing 49%, the highest globally, becoming the fastest growing large spirits market in the world.
Our Response 
We will continue to tap the massive growth opportunity in India while managing the complexity of the alcoholic beverage industry with diverse pricing, regulatory, and route-to-market across the country.
We are strengthening our premium and luxury portfolio by 
expanding established brands like Johnnie Walker and introducing new offerings tailored to local tastes. Innovation remains a key focus, creating new to world products like flavoured spirits, new whiskies for the young LDA consumers, disruptive pack formats, Indian craft spirits as well as investments in the areas of low-alcohol beverages and craft spirits to meet emerging consumer needs. We are also leveraging digital platforms, social media and creating owned platforms to ensure deeper connections with younger LDA consumers. Sustainability is central to our strategy, with initiatives focused on reducing water usage, adopting eco-friendly packaging, and promoting responsible consumption. Additionally, we are expanding our market reach by strengthening distribution networks and transforming retail operations in metros, tier II and tier III cities, where disposable incomes and demand are rising. Strategic partnerships with distributors and retailers further enhance market penetration and brand visibility. Through these initiatives, we aim to reinforce our market leadership while driving long-term, sustainable growth in the evolving Indian market.

and Analysis section on page 219

At Diageo India, our aspiration is to become the best performing, 
most trusted and respected consumer products company in India. This ambition drives us to embed sustainability and ESG principles at the core of our decision-making and business strategies. Our commitment extends beyond financial success, aiming to create a meaningful and positive impact on the planet and its people.
Launched in 2020, the ‘Spirit of Progress’, our ESG action plan, is an enabler of our growth ambition and a commercial 
imperative for our business, underpinned by our commitment to do business the right way. This comprehensive framework outlines clear goals that address the issues most critical to our business and stakeholders. Anchored in three strategic pillars,  it reflects our commitment to environmental stewardship, empowering people, and uplifting communities. By embedding these priorities into our operations, we are building a resilient, future-ready business that creates long-term stakeholder value.

Disciplined Capital Allocation and Prudent 
Financial Management Practices
We pursue healthy financial practices to enhance organisational future-readiness. Our financial strategy prioritises 
profitable growth and a strong balance sheet to enable sustained investment in the future. At its core is a disciplined capital management approach that balances reinvestment in growth opportunities with the maximisation of shareholder returns. 
We achieve this by investing in brands and innovation to drive long-term growth, alongside strategic acquisitions to 
strengthen our portfolio. These initiatives enhance brand equity and support the development of a future-ready business. Value creation for stakeholders is further ensured through a well-defined dividend distribution policy and sustained investments in ‘Spirit of Progress’ initiatives.
In FY 2024-25, we continued to focus on our Revenue Growth Management (RGM) initiatives thereby optimising product mix, pricing, and channel execution to drive value-led growth. This was complemented by continued premiumisation and sustained investment of ` 1,128 Crores in A&P, leading to improved brand visibility and strong momentum in the Luxury & Premium segment. Together, these efforts supported sales volume growth, stronger pricing, and overall revenue growth. On the cost side, we drove efficiencies through scale, best-in-class manufacturing practices, strategic sourcing, and tech-enabled inventory management. Our multi-year supply agility programme further enhanced our operational footprint. These initiatives delivered ` 243 Crores in pricing and revenue growth and ` 388 Crores in enterprise productivity during the year.Revenue and profit maximisation 
The net sales salience 
of the P&A segment increased to 89% in FY 2024-25,  from 87% 
in FY 2023-24 and 65% in FY 2019-20. Through effective brand refresh, engaging marketing activities, and the strength of our unique portfolio, we have delivered an impressive 5-year CAGR of 12% in P&A NSV. 
Working capital and debt management 
Led by our consistent financial performance and prudent capital management, Diageo India became debt free in FY 2022-23. We ensure 
optimal working capital through a sharp focus on better inventory management and improvement in the receivables cycle. Our working capital requirement (as % of NSV) has, resultantly, come down from 21% in FY 2019-20 to 17% in FY 2024-25. 
We continue to hold a position of strength in the industry, with a net worth of ` 7,879 Crores and net cash surplus of ` 3,089 Crores 
(including current investments and term deposits) as on March 31, 2025. This gives us adequate headroom to commit to capex, and also equips us to invest in branding and promotion. Key Performance Indicators*

Commitment to Quality Assurance & Food Safety
At Diageo India, we are committed to upholding 
the highest standards of quality, ensuring our products are safe and consistently meet consumer expectations and aspirations. We adhere to stringent internal quality standards, rigorous processes, and robust quality assurance practices.
Our hygiene and quality protocols are 
uniformly applied across our own and third-party manufacturing facilities. They comply with the requirements of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), as well as relevant state excise regulations and Legal Metrology Rules (LMR).
We employ a comprehensive quality 
management approach that spans product design, raw material sourcing, and final deliveries to consumers and customers. This approach ensures consistent quality assurance and food safety. 
We test our finished products through a 
comprehensive range of physical, chemical, and microbial tests under GPIP (Global Product Integrity Testing Programme). Additionally, our sensory panel members participate in an independent validation scheme, NSSPS (Neutral Spirits Sensory Proficiency Scheme). 
We have also initiated capability building for our 
quality assurance laboratories through third-party validation programmes such as DAPS (Diageo Alcohol Proficiency Scheme).
Quality Assurance from Grain  
to Glass
Quality assurance from grain to glass is at the 
heart of our brands. The continuous improvement of quality and the enhancement of customer and consumer confidence in our brands are key determinants in the long-term success of Diageo India. We employ a comprehensive risk assessment system that spans the entire grain-to-glass journey, ensuring that every stage of the supply chain adheres to our stringent quality standards.
By integrating best-in-class practices, digital 
technologies, global risk management standards, local regulatory requirements, and automation into our systems and processes, we support our efforts with regularly updated quality norms and inspection processes. This holistic approach ensures consistent quality assurance and safety for 
all our products.

are resolved and remaining in progress.Quality Certifications and Recognitions 
At Diageo India, we are committed to delivering products and services that adhere to the highest quality standards. By maintaining crucial 
industry certifications, we consistently meet our customers’ expectations and comply with regulatory requirements.
Our compliance framework is aligned with our Integrated Management System (IMS), encompassing: ISO 9001:2015 — Quality 
Management, ISO 14001:2015 — Environmental Management, ISO 45001:2018 — Occupational Health & Safety. The certifications for all manufacturing facilities is in progress and will be completed in a phased manner.
Our manufacturing sites are certified under FSSC 22000 — a GFSI- recognised food safety certification. Currently, 10 out of 11 own 
manufacturing facilities and 20 out of 25 third-party manufacturing facilities are certified. The certifications for remaining manufacturing facilities is in progress and will be completed in a phased manner.
Our certification process involves:
•

ws to ensure compliance with applicable global internal standards.
• Continuous training programmes f

• Engagement with third-party cer

These certifications reflect our dedication to continuous improvement in quality excellence, safety, and sustainability.Holistic Quality Assurance Framework 
We have a robust supplier management system to ensure our raw materials 
and packaging materials are sourced from approved suppliers to ensure best-in-class quality.Raw & Packaging Materials:
We have a stringent supplier onboarding process, starting with qualification audits, periodic audits, and regular supplier performance management, including supplier handholding and technical support. We also work closely with suppliers to address and resolve issues, ensuring the delivery of the right product to our customers and consumers.Suppliers/vendors
Our FSSAI-certified manufacturing units implement robust systems and 
processes to ensure the delivery of high-quality products. We conduct material inspections upon receipt and monitor quality online throughout the production process. Final product inspections ensure that our products are safe and meet quality standards. Additionally, every truck is inspected before despatch, guaranteeing comprehensive quality checks throughout our operations. We constantly collaborate with our third-party manufacturers with respect to technology and support in areas like system and process changes, capability building of internal teams, and also modifying infrastructure requirements. These interventions demonstrate our focus on delivering the right quality and safe products to our consumers.Manufacturing
In the market, finished goods (FG) quality is assessed impartially under 
Diageo’s Global Distribution Quality Standards (GDQS) by a third-party agency. We also engage an independent agency to conduct annual on-shelf quality assessments and competitor benchmarking. This ensures that quality is monitored throughout the supply chain, with insights integrated back into operations to drive a consumer-focused quality improvement process.Distribution and On Shelf Quality
We also have a robust third-party-managed customer complaint system, where consumers can raise concerns through calls or mails. A tiered governance mechanism ensures prompt redressal of any concern/issue at the root cause, along with corrective actions to prevent recurrence. The insights gathered are then integrated back into operations, driving a consumer-driven quality improvement process.Customer/Consumer Quality Health and Safety: Envisioning 
a Zero Harm Culture
Our commitment to Zero Harm drives 
every decision we make, ensuring the highest standards of safety. Through active engagement, empowerment, and continuous improvement, we foster a workplace where every individual takes ownership of safety. By championing innovation, accountability, and collaboration, we strive to create an environment where risks are minimised and well-being is maximised, ensuring no one gets hurt — whether at the workplace, on the road, or at home.
As part of our safety strategy, we have 
defined key pillars that guide us in our pursuit of safety excellence and our vision of Zero Harm. These focused pillars — Governance, Risk Mitigation and Management, Safety Culture, Digitisation and Analytics, and ERC (Engagement, Recognition and Certifications) — support various programmes and initiatives across our operations. These are led by line managers and supported by site and corporate EHS teams.Our Global Risk Management System (GRMS) is adhered to at all business units, supported by strong governance, including audits and reviews. Leadership at all levels provides visible felt leadership by actively participating in safety reviews, conducting safety walkabouts, and ensuring teams across all locations are engaged through initiatives such as:

Building a Culture of Quality
Fostering a culture of quality is crucial for 
achieving long-term success and ensuring customer/consumer satisfaction. This requires embedding quality at every level of the organisation, making it an intrinsic part of our operations.
Key Pivots to Nurture a Quality 
Culture
Clear Standards & Continuous 
Improvement 
We have comprehensive management 
procedures in place to mitigate quality risks and protect consumers. These include an FSSAI-aligned product recall process and Global risk management standards. Our central and site steering committees monitor this process with the support of a Crisis Management Team (CMT) chaired by the Managing Director and CEO.
Each of our manufacturing lines undergoes 
hourly quality checks via a positive release mechanism. In addition, product mock recalls are conducted annually at every site to ensure emergency preparedness.Distribution quality is monitored at 
select external depots, where 30% of boxes per truck are inspected during unloading, with results reported to Corporate Quality team. These insights are shared with manufacturing sites for learning and action planning. Annual third-party shelf assessments at select retail outlets — including on-shelf quality assessments based on Consumer Relevant Quality Standards (CRQS) — provide valuable insights, including competitor benchmarking. Regular tracking of these quality KPIs ensures consistent delivery of the right product to customers and consumers, supporting both purchase and re-purchase.
Employee Engagement & Capability 
Building 
The organisation-wide quality initiatives at 
Diageo India are driven by a dedicated team of experts. New joiners receive a comprehensive in-house induction and refresher training, which includes various tools and techniques such as Six Sigma certifications. We are also establishing a Centre of Excellence Culture in liquid 
and packaging quality through external agency training and certifications. Additionally, employees are encouraged to attend external trainings to stay updated with the latest developments.
A structured, calendarised ‘Gurukul 
Trainings’ programme is conducted weekly for the entire manufacturing teams, covering aspects of quality, global standards, and internal SOPs to ensure continuous awareness and adherence to quality standards across the organisation.
To foster continuous improvement, we 
engage in regular feedback collection, data analysis, and process optimisation.
Collaboration
We encourage cross-functional collaboration through various review forums to identify issues early, share knowledge, and achieve common quality goals.
Ensuring Regulatory Compliance
Responsible Marketing & Labelling The alcohol industry is highly regulated by federal authorities at the national level, and the excise departments at the respective 
state level. Supported by domain experts, we ensure rigorous compliance with the regulations governing manufacturing and operations. Measures like regular audits and assessments, along with structured employee training programmes, ensure a culture of compliance. 
Our marketing efforts are governed by the Diageo Marketing Code, Digital Code, Responsible Research Global Standard, and 
Data Protection Global Policy. The Diageo Consumer Information Standard sets minimum mandatory labels and packaging requirements for all our brands. It covers metrics like alcohol content by volume, slogans for responsible drinking, recycling and sustainability, ingredients list, and a reference to our global responsible drinking website - DRINKiQ.com. 
We also have in place streamlined processes to ensure that the data used to generate on-pack labelling is compliant with 
applicable regulations and labelling policies. This ensures that clear and accurate ingredient information is provided to consumers to make informed buying decisions. Scaling Operational and Cost-Efficiencies 
The implementation of best-in-class operational practices across our manufacturing systems and processes enables us to consistently deliver high-quality products while maintaining efficiency and optimising working capital. Key measures undertaken across operations include:

Journey towards touchless planning

System (TMS)

Ensuring an Efficient and Responsible Supply Chain
Our robust end-to-end supply chain network ensures the seamless production and distribution of our products. With 47 depots, 280+ 
distributors and 600+ licensed wholesalers, our distribution system ensures sustained and timely product availability across markets. 
We ensure supply chain resilience through a robust process for selecting suppliers based on their ability to effectively deliver services, 
materials, and timelines. This process is guided by our Partnering with Suppliers Standard, which covers key aspects of ethical business practices, human rights protection, health and safety standards, and environmental impact reduction. High- and medium-risk suppliers are also evaluated for business continuity and financial risks. In addition, we have integrated responsible sourcing practices, detailed on  page 126 of this report.
Supply Chain Agility 
Programme 
In FY 2022-23, we launched a multi-
year programme to build a leaner, more reliable, and efficient supply chain designed to enhance Diageo India’s future readiness and competitiveness. A key pillar of this initiative is footprint optimisation to become more asset-light and maximise capital efficiency. From 93 manufacturing facilities in FY 2014-15, we have consolidated operations to 46 by  FY 2021-22 and further to 36 in FY 2024-25. This rationalisation is enabling leaner operations, better resource utilisation, and improved market responsiveness, while also driving higher volume growth. 
We use the FSD (Factory-SKU-Depot) 
linear programming model to optimise our manufacturing and distribution network. The long-term goal is to operate one scaled facility per state to enhance localisation, minimise interstate movement, and reduce associated costs and taxes.
We have also achieved our target of  
co-locating bottling plants with Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) distillation units across all strategic supplier locations. This integration enables streamlined production, reduces transportation costs, and enhances overall supply chain efficiency. Producing the right-quality ENA on-site also improves product consistency and responsiveness to market demand.Investing in the Future 
To support our growth agenda, we have outlined multiple capital expenditure programmes aimed at ensuring future readiness and meeting the rising demand for spirits in India. Key initiatives include:

An unexpected range of Rum, Gin, Vodka McDowell’s is the World’s No. 1 selling whisky, as rated by Drinks 
International Millionaire’s Club 2023 & 2024. It is the only Indian spirit brand in the Kantar BrandZ Most Valuable Indian Brands, ranked at no. 41. Crafted by blending scotch whisky and select Indian malts, McDowell’s brand, with its 125 years legacy, is now deeply entrenched among Yaars (friends) , making it synonymous with friendship and lending it unmatched market leadership over the years. From celebrating the bonds of friendship to enabling Yaars to express and acknowledge their Yaari (friendship), it has created a unique bond with its 25+ Million consumers across the 20 countries where it is enjoyed. The all-new McDowell’s & Co Distiller’s Batch Indian Single Malt whisky redefines McDowell’s legacy for a new era driven by aspirational consumers. Distilled and matured in our Nashik Distillery, this triple-cask whisky represents the pinnacle of Indian whisky craftsmanship and luxury, guided by generations of expertise and commitment to quality. Initially matured in Ex-Bourbon and Virgin Oak Casks, it is then aged in Cabernet Sauvignon and Shiraz casks unique to the Sahyadri terrain, complementing the flavour with an exceptional vintage character. It boasts aromas of vanilla and rich fresh fruit, with gentle citrus and spice afternotes. Its velvety texture reveals complex layers of sweet wood and fresh fruity flavours, resulting in a mellow-sweet and lingering finish.
Its captivating bottle and label design, adorned with deep purple 
tones and veiled peaks, embodies the spirit of the region. Inspired by the breathtaking beauty of the Nashik Distillery, where casks are enveloped by mountain mists, it reflects the vibrant hues and mystical aura of this unique region.

Celebrating Bold Choices Crafted with natural ingredients

convention to craft Royal Challenge (RC), an award-winning, international-quality Indian whisky, matured in a charred American Oak Cask. Anchored on future codes of aspiration and modern status, the brand caters to the consumer’s growing need for responsible and sustainable propositions with its new positioning - ‘One with Nature’. Its new, bold, and distinctive packaging features an iconic green embossed bottle, highlighting its authenticity and premiumness. It reflects the craftmanship of our Master Blender, Louise Martin, who harmoniously blended nature’s finest barley, fresh water and ten imported scotches with aged Indian malts and fine grain spirits, making every sip a revelation and one truly ‘Crafted with natural ingredients’.
The brand’s new proposition embodies newer status codes and 
proposes conscious living as a mark of an evolved mindset and a progressive lifestyle. It inspires people to lead a better, conscious life of enjoyment, celebrating the goodness of nature. This is manifested through Signature Packaged Drinking Water’s partnership with Ziro, India’s No. 1 music festival anchored on sustainability, and support to ‘The Mangrove Replenishment Project’ spread across 60+ acres in Odisha. Godawan
A new world of sustainable, modern,

An enduring legacy of whisky-making
Antiquity Blue embodies timeless grain whisky-making traditions, with roots in the Cameron Bridge Distillery. It is blended with 
scotch from the same distillery, using the process of grain distillation in copper pot stills. The whisky’s rich and inviting colour is inspired by the hue of antique gold. Pronounced malt and rich wood flavours are supplemented with a hint of peat and heather.
All-new Antiquity — an icon reimagined 
With its unrivalled status in India, Antiquity Blue is celebrated among whisky drinkers for its highly rated unique liquid and iconic identity. To resonate with the existing loyal, discerning audience, as well as the new, young legal drinking age whisky consumers seeking distinctive experiences, we have introduced the all-new Antiquity Blue.

Godawan is an artisanal single-malt whisky crafted in Rajasthan, representing the true spirit of the resplendent desert. With the majestic and endangered native Great Indian Bustard as its mark, it pays tribute to the land’s nurturing heritage. Crafted from locally sourced six-row barley, and matured in Rajasthan’s warm, dry climate with temperatures often reaching 100°F, Godawan uses innovative cask architecture and rare Indian botanicals to deliver incredible depth of flavour and it is available in two distinctive expressions: Godawan 01, Rich and Rounded, and Godawan 02, Fruit and Spice.
In 2023, the brand’s journey took a global turn with the launch of Godawan 100 
Collector’s Edition in Rajasthan and Dubai, highlighting the bird’s critical plight and dedicating the proceeds towards its conservation efforts. We also forged an exciting partnership with the Taj Group of Hotels, based on our aligned goal of promoting luxury with a conscience approach. A limited edition of Godawan crafted exclusively for the Taj Palaces was launched at Taj Palace Mumbai.
Aligned with our commitment to the ‘Make in India’ initiative, we partnered with the 
Agricultural & Processed Food Products Export Development Authority, Ministry of Commerce & Development (Govt of India), to jointly showcase Godawan at trade events like Indus Fest (Uttar Pradesh) and IFE London.

Johnnie Walker
The World’s No.1 Scotch whisky
A cultural icon with a 200-year legacy, Johnnie Walker is 
enjoyed and embraced across 180+ countries. Its journey started in 1820 in Kilmarnock, when founder John Walker pushed the boundaries of what whisky could be, and today it is one of the world’s most enjoyed scotches with a strong equity amongst all international whiskies. In the last 25+ years, the brand has continued to inspire with its philosophy and iconic slogan — ‘KEEP WALKING’, deepening its cultural relevance among the next generation of whisky drinkers. 
In India, Johnnie Walker has an iconic presence, right from the 
British Raj era and carried forward in culture through Bollywood cinema. In recent years, the trademark has championed cultural and collective progress by partnering with diverse talent and communities. These extend from local collectives like Aravani Art Project and Echoes of Earth, to global iconic talents like John Legend, Raja Kumari and more, along with marquee music moments like Lollapalooza India etc. This is our entry-level Scotch in the portfolio. It is a delicious result of up to 35 whiskies, including many of Scotland’s most celebrated single malts and grain whiskies from Speyside, Highlands, Islands and Lowlands.
This is a 12-year iconic blend that includes more than 
30 single malts from the four corners of Scotland.
This is a part of our luxury portfolio. It makes a 
statement, perfect for those occasions of celebration and indulgence. A versatile blend, only the finest make the Gold Label Reserve Standard.The latest addition to the Johnnie Walker family, this versatile, well-rounded, and made-for-mixing whisky is crafted using whiskies predominantly matured in first-fill American oak casks. Bursting into life when its sweet, bright, fruity flavours mix with lemonade and orange, it is perfect for golden sundowners and casual moments, best enjoyed when shared with good friends. This new expression captivates both whisky enthusiasts and new drinkers, and also those who enjoy experimenting and mixing drinks for smooth, sessionable drinks beyond classic scotch. 
It is a rare flavour and the pinnacle of luxury. Only 1 in 10,000 casks has the richness and character required to craft this liquid. There are layers here, and as you taste it you experience each of it in waves. With Blue, there’s always something more to discover.Currently, Johnnie Walker Scotch Whisky caters to diverse segments of affluent India, with offerings across price points and taste preferences for different consumers. From Red Label as the entry level Scotch to the iconic and popular Black Label, to the special occasion Gold Label Reserve, to the ultimate luxury icon in Blue Label, and more recently a refreshing and flavourful Scotch designed specifically for the preferences of younger LDA consumers, Johnnie Walker Blonde. As a pioneer of ‘Scotch drinking culture’ in India, the brand is dialling up its play in contemporary culture appealing to the next generation of luxury consumers. Efforts include introducing a variety of blends and curated experiences at leading bars and music festivals and being at the forefront of modern retail transformation to create standout off-trade visibility. With this, Johnnie Walker continues to elevate how the brand is experienced and perceived by consumers. Johnnie Walker Red Label

The Singleton Don Julio 
Slow batch distilled, a whisky worth savouring!World’s celebrated luxury tequila, now in India
Slow-crafted with care and passion, the Singleton is a balanced single malt whisky that is easy to drink and deliciously enjoyable. It is made by hand selecting and malting our own barley, carefully applying long fermentation and slow batch distillation, and expertly harmonising the flavours of both European and American oak casks. This makes the Singleton a uniquely versatile single malt that will take you back to Scotland. Singleton breaks away from formal and serious traditional single malt, offering an accessible, informal and casual appeal that resonates with modern trends and new consumers. The brand was founded in 1942 by Don Julio González-Frausto Estrada at the ‘La Primavera’ distillery in Jalisco highlands of Mexico. Dedicated to producing high-quality tequila and setting new benchmarks in supremacy, he planted each agave apart, to allow proper room to grow and fully mature before harvesting. 
Continuing this legacy, the tequila is today crafted using only the highest-calibre, fully matured and ripened blue agave, hand-selected 
from the Los Altos region’s rich clay soils. The use of traditional methods, including brick ovens for cooking and copper pot stills for distillation, lends an extraordinary flavour to this tequila. This dedication to craftsmanship sets it apart from mass-produced tequila, making it the choice of choice for the crème de la crème of the film, fashion, music and art fraternity globally.
With the massive surge in the desire for luxury consumption among India’s rising new class of luxury explorers who appreciate 
exceptional quality, we have introduced Don Julio’s portfolio — Blanco, Reposado, Anejo, and the iconic luxury spirit 1942 — in India. An essential must-have at parties and the ultimate drink of choice, it made a mark with a star-studded launch, and is set to craft unforgettable experiences.

World’s No. 1 Vodka brand
Smirnoff is globally renowned for its quality and unique manufacturing process, involving three distillations and 10 stages of charcoal filtration. From its launch in Russia in 1864 by Vladimir Smirnoff, to its re-establishment in Europe over a century ago and entry in America in 1934, the brand has survived and thrived through the decades. Initiating the 50s cocktail revolution and revolutionising the 90s club culture, it is still the drinker’s and bartender’s choice across the globe. Through the years, it has championed inclusive cultures, shaped defining moments in the film and showbiz industry, fuelled EDM’s rise, and differentiated itself with the largest range of flavours globally. 
More recently, the brand is re-inventing itself to connect with 
the next generation through a globally consistent brand idea of ‘We Do We’ speaking to their ethos.
In addition, we’ve launched three new exciting flavours (Minty 
Jamun, Mango Mirchi and Zesty Lime) in line with local taste preferences of the Indian consumers.

An AI-powered Commercial Tech Ecosystem Built 
for the Future of Sales
Our new-age Salesforce application delivers intelligent prompt 
nudges, digitises trade spends, and leverages advanced image recognition to drive in-market excellence.
Designed to scale across channels, it empowers both On-Trade  and 
Off-Trade  teams with data-driven agility, precision, and performance.Way forwardpoint of sale or purchase. It enables them to authenticate their 
bottle of choice and learn about the source history of every component of the finished product. This is currently activated for five of our brands. The batch-specific data is uploaded on a server which eventually helps us run a batch-specific identification of any bottle through OCR-based reading of the back labels, which can be done with the help of a mobile phone using a specific pre-installed TRAG app. This process helps our consumers or internal investigators or Quality executives to obtain feedback on authentication of the bottle, and also get a view of the brand and product provenance. This technology has been adopted because state excise departments do not allow application of an additional QR code on the primary packaging, Hence, OCR-based reading of the back label turns out to be a frugal and technologically reliable alternative for connected packaging for the Indian Spirits Industry at large, and for Diageo India specifically. While QR codes on primary packaging is not allowed in most of the states, an exception has been made in West Bengal as a joint action between State Excise department and the Brand owner where we have been allowed to incorporate a consumer interfacing masked dynamic QR code that enables the consumer to interact with the QR code and obtain an authentication message back on mobile phone. We have been first to implement this as an additional label on the bottle which is now getting integrated directly onto the label through online printing of variable QR codes.

of sustainable growth, we have deployed innovative connected packaging technology to drive meaningful change in society. The initiative includes integrating QR codes to transform our packaging into an interactive platform for consumer engagement. Through this, consumers can gain insight into product authenticity and its environmental journey, sourcing details, and recycling instructions. The initiative aims to empower consumers to make informed and environmentally responsible choices. 
This initiative involves the digital integration of scannable back 
labels with batch-related data uploaded to a third-party server, making all relevant information available to consumers at the Critical Control Points (CCP) monitoring and management through SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) systems allow real-time data capture and automated control across production processes.
Leveraging QR technology allows for real-time tracking of casks, ensuring better inventory control, traceability, and 
process efficiency.
Automated blending systems use advanced algorithms and RFID/QR tagging to identify and utilise the right casks for blending.AI-driven production planning systems analyse market demand and available production capacity to create dynamic and 
efficient schedules.
AI-powered vision systems enable automated inspection of bottles, labels, and packaging.Real-time monitoring systems are integrated with key production equipment to track and improve overall equipment effectiveness. QR code tagging of finished goods allows seamless tracking of batch information across the supply chain.Vision Management Systems (VMS) automate the putaway process in warehouses by identifying and allocating the optimal 
storage locations.
Order management systems generate picklists based on the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle.Internet of Things (IoT) solutions are deployed for line monitoring and inspection, providing actionable insights into 
production processes.

OHSSAI — EHS and Sustainability Gold Star Awards 
Kumbalgodu, Karnataka
Nimapara, OdishaAlwar, Rajasthan
Malkajgiri, TelanganaHealth and Safety Framework
Our Health Safety & Well-being policy encapsulates our 
responsibility to protect the workplace health, safety, and wellbeing of our people. We follow our Global Risk Management Standards (GRMS) for Health and Safety, comprising 54 standards that apply to all our locations. Our 11 Safety Standards (SFIP), Severe & Fatal Prevention Programme, and 11 critical, non-negotiable Life Saving Rules aim to eliminate severe and fatal incidents from our operations.
Our Safety Management system is in accordance with ISO 45001 
requirements. The Nashik Unit is certified to ISO 45001, and other sites are in the process of certification for the Integrated Management System (IMS) covering EHSQ, ISO 45001, ISO 14001, and ISO 9001. We also influence and encourage third-party manufacturers to enhance their safety management systems and pursue external certifications. Currently, two units are ISO 45001 certified, while three units are in the certification process.
In FY 2024-25, four of our units were awarded EHS and 
sustainability awards by prestigious organisations and foundations, a testament to our mature EHS management system and leadership in workplace safety and environmental stewardship.Focus on Safety Culture and  
Visible Felt leadership
Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, 
Training and Incident InvestigationGovernance, Safety  
Assessments and AuditsSafety Communication, Engagement  
and Continual ImprovementAs part of the organisation’s Zero Harm vision, where no one gets hurt at the workplace, on roads, or at home, a focused programme 
has been deployed to build a safety behaviour culture through Safe Behaviour Observations (SBO). This programme is led by line managers who provide visible felt leadership by conducting periodic safety walkabouts in the work area, observing safe and at-risk behaviours, identifying unsafe conditions, and engaging directly with workers on safety practices. In the long run, the Behaviour-Based Safety (BBS) process helps foster a strong, safe work culture.
Our health and safety standard incorporates hazard 
identification, risk assessment, and incident investigation as core processes. We continually monitor health and safety parameters using both leading and lagging safety indicators. We have an established practice of documented reporting of work-related hazards through the Safety Information Report Card (SIRC), which is used by all employees. All employees are encouraged to report and eliminate work-related hazards that could cause injury or ill health.
We also provide regular training to help employees identify and 
report unsafe conditions and near misses, investigate work-related incidents, and assess residual risks following corrective actions.A formal Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) process is conducted for all activities, with any gaps identified through these assessments promptly addressed. All incidents are investigated, and lessons learned are shared across the organisation as part of our learning culture and horizontal deployment.Diageo India has established mature health and safety review systems at all levels, along with a structured audit mechanism. This starts with a predefined schedule of self-assessments by all units against Global Risk Management Standards (GRMS), identifying areas for improvement and drawing up action plans to close gaps, which are tracked and monitored in various review meetings. In addition, Site Heads conduct focused reviews on a monthly basis through Manufacturing Operation Reviews (MOR) and Management Review Meetings (MRM). The organisation continually carries out internal and external audits on various safety themes, including SFIP audits, ISO audits, risk-based audits such as electrical audits, in-plant traffic risk assessments, thermography, and fire risk surveys, among others. These are planned based on identified risks and improvement plans at each location.We have a robust process for communication, engagement, and continual improvement in safety across the organisation. In manufacturing units, as part of daily work management, T1 reviews take place on the shop floor every day, where all shop floor team members conduct a focused review under SQDCMS (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Morale, and Sustainability). Safety is the first discussion point, and any safety concern is brought to everyone’s attention and addressed immediately. As part of Department Head reviews (T2 reviews), safety is also discussed, and finally, during Unit Management Reviews (T3 reviews), the overall status of safety is monitored. Additionally, each unit has a Central Safety Committee with equal representation from workers and management, chaired by the Unit Head. Along with reviewing various safety and health KPIs, this committee serves as an escalation forum for any pending or unattended workplace hazard concerns. All actions are minuted and tracked through to closure.
A monthly safety campaign is conducted on one of the 
SFIP standards, engaging all employees through various interventions, including awareness sessions on these safety standards.
•
 We continually improv
e safety in the workplace by 
reducing risk and eliminating hazards through various 
mechanisms such as Kaizen, One Page Learning, Safety Action Meetings (SAM), Focused Improvement (FI) projects using the DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve, Control) framework, and Yellow and Green Belt projects. We also monitor and close out Safety Improvement Report Cards (SIRC), where unsafe conditions and near misses are identified and reported by shop floor team members.
•
 Each Diageo India site conducts regular t
own halls 
where monthly safety performance is communicated to employees. In addition, each site runs various training programmes, some targeted to specific employee groups and others open to all employees.

Pioneer Grain-to-Glass Sustainability
Preserve Water for Life
Water, a precious shared resource, is essential to our existence, from its use in farming to the distillation process, and is under increasing 
pressure, with scarcity in many parts of the world, including India. Our water stewardship strategy is based on the best practices across four areas: operations, supply chain, communities, and advocacy. We undertake community projects to achieve our goal of replenishing more water than we use in our direct operations. 
1. Water Replenishment
Through our water conservation efforts, we focus on increasing the availability of water for productive use. 
Various water replenishment projects, 
including desilting community ponds, constructing rainwater harvesting structures and check dams, enhanced the availability of water for the local communities in the catchment.
In FY 2024-25, we initiated projects to 
replenish 182K Cu.M. of water across various regions, including Nanded (Maharashtra), Nashik (Maharashtra), Hardoi (Uttar Pradesh) and Alwar (Rajasthan).
Collective action on water 
Diageo India is taking collective action in its priority water-stressed basins through a multi-stakeholder collaboration to address broader systemic water risks. 
The Godavari River basin in Maharashtra 
is a priority for us, considering its significance for the state. Over the past five years, we have implemented various projects across catchment areas in Nashik and Nanded, including rainwater harvesting, desilting of ponds, and Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) initiatives, to ensure water sustainability.
We are the founding partner of The 
Godavari Initiative (TGI), launched in Mumbai in FY 2024-25, to promote sustainable management of the Godavari River Basin, benefiting 23 Million people across 9 districts in Maharashtra. TGI, along with Diageo India’s water replenishment programme, will help address water scarcity at scale and contribute to achieving a net-positive water impact. Recently, TGI successfully hosted its first regional consultation at Nashik, the Godavari River’s origin, attracting eminent regional industry associations and corporates. 
2. Water Sanitation and Hygiene 
(WASH) Initiatives for Healthier Communities
A part of our grain-to-glass initiatives, 
we focus on improving Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) facilities in the local communities. We have been able to transform individual lives significantly, by Given our business’s strong dependence on natural resources and its direct exposure to risks from climate change, water stress, and biodiversity loss, we have prioritised sustainability across our value chain. Sustainable development is a central pillar of our ‘Spirit of Progress’ action plan. With a strong focus on water efficiency and reducing our carbon footprint, we actively engage with communities to address these challenges and adopt sustainable solutions.SDGs Impacted
providing sanitation facilities and clean drinking water across Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Meghalaya, Odisha, Rajasthan. This has led to the adoption of safer sanitary practices and promotion of the overall well-being of the communities.
Accelerate to a Low-carbon 
World
1. Afforestation and Plantation
To drive carbon sequestration, we have 
directed our efforts towards maintenance of more than 200K trees that were planted in FY 2023-24. Additionally, we have planted 46K trees across two states during FY 2024-25. 
2. Regenerative Agriculture 
Our regenerative agriculture programme, launched in Punjab and Haryana, seeks to promote the adoption of sustainable, best practices among smallholder farmers. It includes training on direct seeding, crop residue management, efficient irrigation, improved soil health and agroforestry. The programme seeks to transform existing agricultural practices in the region into a more sustainable model.
Case Study
The Challenge
In Maharashtra’s Dindori block in Nashik, women from marginalised tribal communities face deep-rooted economic hardships due to landless farming, rainfed agriculture, and limited employment opportunities. Their meagre incomes often fall short of meeting basic needs, pushing them into debt or forcing migration to cities for informal labour, which heightens emotional and financial strain.
The Intervention
To address these challenges, Diageo India, in partnership with Savitribai Phule Mahila Ekatma Samaj Mandal and S4S Technologies, introduced solar-powered food processing units. The initiative trained women to process unsold or lower-grade produce – such as tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and onions – into value-added products like dried powder and sauces for the food and beverage sector. It also equipped them with technical skills and entrepreneurial training, enabling them to run micro-enterprises with dignity.
Diageo India contributed 10% of the seed capital, 
while the remaining 90% was facilitated through loans by S4S Technologies. Training in equipment handling and group-based operations enhanced team efficiency and helped create a strong support network.Empowering Women Through Hospitality 
and Enterprise Development
‘Learning for Life’ is Diageo India’s flagship business and hospitality skills programme, aimed at 
individuals facing barriers to employment. By providing equal access to vocational training and resources, the programme enhances employability, improves livelihoods, and promotes a more inclusive hospitality sector in alignment with our ‘Spirit of Progress’ goals.
It has helped increase the monthly household income of these women 
by `5,000– `7,000, which is directly credited to their bank accounts. This 
financial independence has dramatically improved household stability, access to education and healthcare, and reduced the need for migration. 
Beyond economic gains, the initiative restored a sense of pride 
and emotional security, truly transforming lives through dignified, sustainable livelihoods.

Fostering an Inclusive and 
Diverse Supply Chain 
At Diageo India, we believe that diversity of perspectives and 
experience drives growth and innovation. Fostering a diverse supplier base is essential for achieving agility, fresh ideas, experiences and cost efficiencies, accelerating product and process innovations. 
What Defines a Diverse Supplier for us?
A diverse supplier is a company that is owned and operated by one or more individuals from traditionally underrepresented minority groups, including, women, people with disabilities, LGBTQIA+, ethnic minorities, or any other underrepresented group.

FY 2024-25Our robust supplier selection process ensures that partners align with Diageo India’s ESG commitments while delivering quality services and 
materials. All high-risk suppliers are screened for labour standards, human rights (including child labour), and legal compliance such as fair pay. We have embedded our ‘Spirit of Progress’ and Responsible Sourcing programme into supplier contracts and bidding processes. Additionally, our rewards and recognition programme incentivises suppliers to continuously enhance their ESG performance, in line with our Partnering with Suppliers Standard.Supplier Screening and Audits
As mandated by our Responsible Sourcing programme. All medium and high-risk supply chain partners are required to register with SEDEX and complete its Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ). High-risk suppliers undergo independent audits as per the SMETA four-pillar audit protocol or its equivalent. 
Our suppliers’ sustainability performance and progress on ESG 
goals are regularly reviewed by a cross-functional team, the CSR & ESG Committee, the Executive Committee, and the CEO, ensuring the highest standards of supply chain operations. While we support and guide our suppliers in improving their operations and ESG compliance, we follow a zero-tolerance policy towards repeat non-compliance and terminate our business relationship with those having recurring non-compliances.Respecting Human Rights Across Value Chain
As a signatory to the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGP) since 2014, we remain committed to safeguarding and promoting human rights across our supply chain. Our Human Rights Global Policy and Partnering with Suppliers Standard explicitly articulate our expectations from our supply chain partners to act in accordance with the UNGP and ILO’s core recommendations and conventions. We undertake comprehensive Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA), prioritising risks based on global mapping process and covering our entire value chain, from tier one suppliers to primary producers such as farmers. violations with fines or penaltiesIncidents of non-compliance  in FY 2024-25The Diageo Marketing Code (DMC) encapsulates our well-
structured approach towards governing all our marketing communications. The code is reviewed bi-annually for continuous industry and market alignment. 
DMC is also designed to prevent marketing to consumers below 
the legal purchase age (LPA) or under 25 years, whichever is higher. A four-layer system is in place to ensure that our marketing campaigns target only LPA+ consumers. The system covers media planning and governance, use of verified logged-in data from platforms with inferred age modelling, layering of inferred data (applies demographic and interest-based targeting), and third-party verification. 
Stringent adherence to applicable laws is ensured by our cross-
functional teams. Our marketing, legal, brand technical, and regulatory functions review the packaging and labelling of new products, while market-based teams, including general managers, assess the communication effectiveness and optimise the organisation’s marketing campaigns. Responsible brand marketing is further ensured through rigorous self-regulation, in compliance with a clearly laid down SOP for gate keeping and approval of marketing and communications material before it is deployed in any of the marketing channels.
